heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF KATINGAN

PROVINCE OF CENTRAL KALIMANTAN

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF KATINGAN REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Katingan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Katingan.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Katingan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public and or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Violence against women is any action or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, mentally, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or private life.
11. Victims of violence against women and children are individuals or groups who experience misery and or suffering as a result of violence and or threats of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will, is or has occurred.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution/organization/agency providing services to victims of violence against women and children who is trained or has expertise in accordance with their competence and authority in providing assistance to victims of violence in accordance with the type of service provided.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions and/or legal apparatus which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence in accordance with their competence and authority.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a functional technical implementation unit as the organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination and other problems.
20. Standard Operating Procedures, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, psychological recovery/services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards, abbreviated as SPM, are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing complaint handling services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, psychological recovery/services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
heading_path: CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES, OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE OF REGULATION
translated_text:
Article 3

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children;
b. protect women and children and provide services to women and Children victims of violence; and
c. empower women and Children victims of violence.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES, OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE OF REGULATION

heading: CHAPTER III
Article 6
heading_path: CHAPTER III
VICTIMS' RIGHTS
translated_text:
Article 6

Child victims of violence, in addition to receiving the rights as referred to in Article 5, also receive special rights as follows:
a. respect for survival, growth and development;
b. to education, health and access to parents during the handling process; and
c. to receive equal protection related to status, citizenship, race, skin color, gender, language, religion, politics, disability, birth or other status.

heading: CHAPTER IV
Article 8
heading_path: CHAPTER IV
AUTHORITY, OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
translated_text:
Article 8

1. The community may participate and be responsible in services, prevention, assistance, recovery and monitoring of victims of violence.
2. Community participation and responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized in the form of:
a. preventing acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

heading: CHAPTER V
CHAPTER VI
Article 11
heading_path: CHAPTER VI
MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obliged to establish Social Protection Houses and or Safe Houses.
2. Social Protection Houses and or Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (1) are to ensure the implementation of UPTD PPA services.
3. For the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may utilize social protection houses and or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The Regent is responsible for making reports on the implementation of SPM through UPTD PPA, submitted to the Governor with copies submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
3. The form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
CHAPTER X
CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

FUNDING

Article 16

Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence are sourced from:
a. State Budget;
b. Regional Budget; and
c. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 17

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Katingan Regency.

Enacted in Kasongan

Promulgated in Kasongan

on 16 January 2023

KATINGAN,

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KATINGAN REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KATINGAN REGENCY

NUMBER 1 OF 2023 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KATINGAN REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, women who play a role as mothers who give birth to healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's ideals.

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in a Regional Regulation.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, implementation, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women in Katingan Regency.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KATINGAN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of the basic rights of victims.

Letter b
What is meant by "justice" is a state where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to achieve welfare.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.

Letter d
What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is all the best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter e
What is meant by "local wisdom" is good cultural values that exist in Katingan society.

Letter f
What is meant by "the right to life, survival and development of children" is a moral principle that every person has the right to live, maintain life and their existence, and improve their standard of living.

Letter g
What is meant by "respect for the victim's opinion" is that the government recognizes and ensures that victims can express their opinions and are given the opportunity to express their views freely on everything that affects them.

Letter h
What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.
